# tobii-linux

Experimental native Eye Tracker 5 head-pose driver

The goal is a native Linux driver for the Tobii Eye Tracker 5 that gives
Star Citizen head tracking under Wine. **The Linux session produces head pose
from a real tracker, and under a patched Wine the Star Citizen Tobii DLL finds
the Linux service and receives its samples. Star Citizen itself has not been
run, and testing so far used WSL2 with usbipd rather than a native Linux
machine.**

Everything here is rebuilt from Tobii's installed binaries and the tracker on
the Windows reference host `albedo`. No other ET5 driver project was used. Most
components are checked against the original machine code by emulating it on
synthetic inputs; those checks are listed in the linked documents.

## What exists

| Stage | Module | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| USB transport, channel framing | `crates/tobii-usb` (`usb.py`, `usb_framing.py`, `usb_channel.py`) | Works on a real tracker; TTP runs on channel 0 |
| TTP requests and replies | `crates/tobii-protocol` (`ttp.py`, `ttp_commands.py`, `ttp_fields.py`) | Startup, unlock, realm, hardware info and stream commands match the original encoders and parsers |
| Camera calibration reply | `crates/tobii-protocol` (`camera_info.py`) | Parser matches the original and reads the live reply |
| Image frames | `crates/tobii-protocol` (`frames.py`) | 280x280 frames at about 33 Hz from a real tracker |
| Face finder | `face_detect.py` | Matches the original detector end to end, network input included |
| Tracking loop and working view | `face_tracking.py` | Working view matches the original; LBF eye refinement not yet run |
| D1 landmarks, confidence gate | `d1.py`, `d1_quality.py` | Crop and gate match the original |
| Face-model fit | `pose_*.py` | Updates, bounds, staged and temporal callers match the original |
| Output conversion, geometry, smoothing | `pose_output.py`, `pose_geometry.py`, `head_pose_pipeline.py` | Euler conversion, geometry stage and One Euro filters match the original |
| Device session and CLI | `crates/tobii-device` (`driver.py`, `streams.py`, `supervisor.py`), `cli.py` | Runs against a real tracker; head pose within about 1% of the Windows depth |
| Game client protocol (PRP) | `prp.py`, `prp_session.py`, `prp_service.py` | Codecs and handshake match the game DLL; service replies match the real service byte for byte |
| Wine pipe bridge | `tools/prp_bridge/` | The game DLL and `tobii_stream_engine.dll` receive tracker samples under Wine |
| Wine pipe listing | `patches/wine/` | Needed for service discovery; tested on Wine 11.0 and master |

With a person holding still, the Linux pipeline and the Windows runtime agree
within 2 mm in position and 0.4 degrees in rotation, and those samples reach
the game DLL's head-tracking API under Wine
([tracking loop](docs/face-tracking.md#fitting-coordinates-live-comparison)).

## Use

The protocol, USB and device layers are Rust crates under `crates/`, loaded by
the Python package as `tobii_linux._native`. Build the extension once after a
checkout and after Rust changes (Rust 1.90 or later and Cargo):

```sh
make native
```

Probe for the tracker (no interface is claimed):

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tobii_linux.cli probe
```

Experimental head-pose session. It needs NumPy and OpenVINO, Tobii's
head-tracking models, and the display area in millimetres in Stream Engine's
corner order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left). The models are not part of this
project and it does not produce them. Put a models/tobii-et5 layout in
`models/tobii-et5` (ignored by Git), in `~/.local/share/tobii-linux/models` or
in the directory `TOBII_LINUX_MODELS` names ([models](models/README.md)):

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tobii_linux.cli headpose \
  --display -296.62 326 111.82 300.38 326 111.82 -296.62 10.27 -3.1
```

It prints one JSON line per camera frame. Frames saved by
`tools/linux_session_probe.py --until frames` can be replayed offline with
`tools/replay_frames.py <log> <frames-dir>`.

A browser demo shows the camera with the face landmarks, head pose, the
tracker's gaze and the device status from one tracker session. It serves
http://localhost:8765/ and also runs in WSL2, where a Windows browser reaches it
through mirrored networking; `--replay-frames` and `--replay-gaze` play recorded
logs without a tracker ([demo](docs/demo.md)):

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tobii_linux.demo
```

`tobii-linux setup` walks through what Tobii's setup does on Windows, on one
browser page it opens itself: the display setup when the tracker has none,
the eye positioning check, the calibration and a named profile. It asks
before writing a display setup and puts the previous calibration back when
it is cancelled; `--simulate unmapped` tries the pages without a tracker
([setup flow](docs/setup-flow.md)):

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tobii_linux.setup
```

## Star Citizen under Wine

Three pieces are needed:

1. A Wine build with the named-pipe listing patch, so the game's Tobii DLL can
   discover the service: `patches/wine/apply.sh <wine-source>` for Wine 10.0
   or later, wine-staging, wine-tkg and LUG runners, and Proton 9 to 11 or
   GE-Proton (it picks the matching variant), then build Wine as usual
   ([details](docs/wine-pipe-enumeration.md)). The game's integration layer
   only tracks discovered trackers, so this is not optional; stock Proton
   lists pipes only partially and is not enough either. The exception is the
   experimental `serve --tet-tcp` route, which the game DLL finds on TCP and
   which gets head pose over a pipe opened by name, so it works with a stock
   runner; it has run under an unpatched Wine with recorded tracker data, not
   yet with the real tracker ([tet-tcp route](docs/tet-tcp.md)).
2. The service on Linux, with the same display area as above:

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tobii_linux.cli serve \
     --display -296.62 326 111.82 300.38 326 111.82 -296.62 10.27 -3.1
   ```

   It serves the tracker's gaze from the same session as well; `--no-gaze`
   serves head pose only. The bridge tells the service which clock the game's
   Wine counter follows (`--wine-clock auto`) and which monitor is primary
   inside the prefix; if
   the game runs on another monitor, pass that monitor's id with
   `--display-id` ([game integration layer](docs/game-integration-layer.md)).
3. The bridge in the game's Wine prefix. `tools/prp_bridge/tobii-linux-wine-run`
   starts it with the game: put it in front of the game command, as a Lutris
   command prefix, in Steam's launch options or in a launch script
   ([launching games](docs/game-launch.md)):

   ```sh
   tobii-linux-wine-run --start-service %command%          # Steam, Proton
   tobii-linux-wine-run wine "C:\...\RSI Launcher.exe"     # plain Wine
   ```

   Build the bridge with `make -C tools/prp_bridge` (MinGW-w64) or
   `nix/bridge.nix`.

See [the bridge document](docs/prp-bridge.md) for the protocol and test
results. Under a patched Wine 11.0, the game DLL's integration layer
receives every sample from the service; Star Citizen itself has not been run.

## Tests

```sh
make native
PYTHONPATH=.local/inference:src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
PYTHONPATH=.local/python:.local/inference:src python3 tools/<oracle>.py
cargo test --workspace
```

`make test`, `make oracles` and `make rust-lint` run the same with the
extension rebuilt first ([Rust core](docs/rust.md)).

The oracles need the private Windows binaries under `evidence/private/` and
the Unicorn emulator; unit tests skip what they cannot run.

## NixOS

```sh
nix build path:.#default
```

Import `inputs.tobii-linux.nixosModules.default` and set
`hardware.tobii-eye-tracker-5.enable = true;` to install the command,
`tobii-linux-wine-run` with the bridge (x86-64), and a udev
rule granting the active seat user access to `2104:0313`. `nix/wine.nix` is an
overlay with patched nixpkgs Wine builds for Lutris
([launching games](docs/game-launch.md#nixos)). To run the game
service in the background as a systemd user service:

```nix
hardware.tobii-eye-tracker-5.headPoseService = {
  enable = true;
  displayArea = [ (-296.62) 326 111.82 300.38 326 111.82 (-296.62) 10.27 (-3.1) ];
};
```

The service reads the models from `~/.local/share/tobii-linux/models` of the
user it runs as; `headPoseService.models` names another directory.

For the Tobii Experience app (tray icon, on/off, the Eye tracking page and
the gaze preview), which runs the same service from login whether or not a
game is running and starts the app with the graphical session:

```nix
hardware.tobii-eye-tracker-5.experience.enable = true;
```

Sessions without `graphical-session.target` (Hyprland without uwsm) start it
with `exec-once = tobii-linux-experience`; Tobii's guest shortcut becomes
`bind = CTRL SHIFT, F10, exec, tobii-linux-experience --guest`
([launching games](docs/game-launch.md#tobii-experience)). The app has not run
against a real tracker yet; [the live checklist](docs/experience-live-checklist.md)
lists what to check.

The flake and module evaluate (`nix flake check` includes a module
evaluation), but no NixOS machine has run them yet.
